entry.entry_asserted: The firm post presents the seed as its investment in Relay, and no pre-seed is reported anywhere (TechCrunch, UKTN, businesscloud). Caveat: businesscloud says 'The round was led by existing investors Project A Ventures and Prologis Ventures', so Project A's money may predate the Nov 2023 announcement (an earlier close of the same seed, or an unannounced pre-seed).

graduation.quote: Relay has now raised a $35 million Series A round led by London-based VC, Plural

relay.status_detail: Operating; USD 35M Series A in Feb 2025 with Project A participating. The pack's 'Wonder acquires Relay' (Apr 2024, NYC restaurant delivery) and 'Relay raises $32.2M Series B' (May 2024, US SMB banking) are namesakes; so is Spark's Relay Payments.
relay.notes: Project A co-led the seed (firm post, TechCrunch) and joined the Plural-led Series A ('participation from Germany's Project A'). The businesscloud 'existing investors' wording is the only hint of an earlier cheque. Logistics is filed as Consumer & Marketplaces, as Packfleet is in sibling books.

saatchi-art.name: Saatchi Art (Saatchi Online, Inc.)

entry.amount: Round total USD 6.15M sold of a USD 10.5M offering (Form D, first sale 2013-04-02); Project A's share not stated
entry.quote: Project A has been involved with Saatchi Online since January 2013 as both an investor and a source of operational expertise
entry.entry_asserted: Firm post (Dec 2013) dates Project A's involvement to Jan 2013, 'Partnering with Balderton Capital', and quotes Balderton as 'the first institutional investor'. The Form D (first sale 2013-04-02, 2 investors) matches the firm archive's dateOfInvestment 2013-04-02. No document names the round: CMS says series_a, the 2016-2024 archive says Series B; vendor Tracxn calls it Series A (not citable).

graduation.not_applicable: entry round unnamed; company sold Aug 2014 with no later round found

saatchi-art.status_detail: Demand Media (Nasdaq) acquired Saatchi Online Inc. for about USD 17M in cash and stock, Aug 2014 (later Leaf Group, bought by Graham Holdings in 2021).
saatchi-art.notes: Project A's entry was the 2013 round with Balderton (Form D USD 6.15M, first sale 2 Apr 2013), but no primary source names it; the firm's own labels disagree (CMS Series A, archive Series B). Form D gives the address as Santa Monica, CA.

shirtagram.name: Shirtagram

entry.quote: Shirtagram is an app that allows you to easily create custom made Christmas presents using your iPhone.
entry.entry_asserted: Shirtagram appears only as a tile on Project A's May 2013 portfolio page (linking shirtagram-app.com); it is gone from the Dec 2013 capture. No firm post, press item, register entry or filing names a company, round or date. It reads like a seasonal (Christmas 2012) app project from Project A's company-builder period rather than a financed company.

shirtagram.status_detail: Circumstantial only: the app's domain lapsed and was re-registered in Feb 2026 by an unrelated party, Project A dropped the tile after May 2013, and no news exists. No company register entry was found, so there is no filing-grade shutdown.
shirtagram.notes: Likely an internal Project A app experiment (photo-to-merchandise gifts, US and Europe delivery) and possibly not a membership at all. The judge should decide membership before stage.

tictail.name: Tictail

entry.lead: Project A Ventures (sole new investor named)
entry.quote: Project A Ventures, a Berlin-based company builder, invests 600,000 euros in the Swedish start-up, Tictail.
entry.entry_asserted: Firm post of 12 Nov 2013 announces Project A joining existing investors Balderton and Klaus Hommels; the Oct 2012 EUR 1.2M seed it describes names only Balderton, Hommels and advisors. The post does not name the round: the live CMS word is 'seed', the 2013-2024 archive says 'Venture Round'.

rounds.source: FashionNetwork USA headline 2015-07-30 'Tictail receives $22 million Series B funding' (pack news line, not re-fetched)

graduation.quote: $8 million Series A funding round lead by Thrive Capital, New York; and followed by early backers Balderton Capital, London; Project A Ventures, Berlin

tictail.notes: Project A's EUR 600k came between the Oct 2012 seed and the Feb 2014 Series A and no document names that round; TechCrunch's Series A article does not name Project A, but Balderton's post does. Tictail also ran a New York office from 2014 (Balderton's book puts HQ in New York).

twig.name: Twig (Twig Bio Ltd)

zenguard.name: ZenGuard (ZenMate)

entry.quote: Berlin-based company builder provides a mid six-figure amount as seed investment
entry.entry_asserted: Firm post of 21 Oct 2013 announces Project A investing in ZenGuard; the Oct 2014 Series A post quotes Horstmann: 'We invested in ZenMate almost one year ago.'

graduation.quote: ZenMate today announced its Series-A funding round of a $3.2m led by influential German internet investors Holtzbrinck Ventures
